## CapEx vs. OpEx budgeting: why one model helps


Capital expenditures ([CapEx](https://www.abacum.ai/glossary/capital-expenditures-capex) ) fund long-term assets such as equipment, buildings, and technology infrastructure. They are capitalized on the balance sheet and depreciated over time. Operating expenses ([OpEx](https://www.abacum.ai/glossary/operating-expense-opex) ) cover the ongoing cost of running the business, such as salaries, rent, utilities, and subscriptions, and they are expensed on the income statement.


The distinction affects financial reporting, tax treatment, and cash flow planning. When capital and operating budgets live in separate files, department leaders can be unsure which category applies, approvals take longer, and operations teams work from older numbers. Many teams still run capital requests through emailed spreadsheets, sometimes tidied up with a general AI tool. It's quick, but nobody can see remaining budget in real time, and the approved number lives in someone's inbox. Planning both in one governed model gives everyone the same picture and ties each plan back to the P&L.


## What to look for in CapEx and OpEx budgeting software


-


**Clear capital and operating views.** See each category by department, project, and period.


-


**Approval workflows.** Route requests and re-forecasts to the right approvers, with a record of who approved what.


-


**Role-based sharing.** Give operations leaders their own approved budgets without exposing the full company plan.


-


**Live actuals.** Connect to your ERP and accounting system so remaining budget updates as spend posts.


-


**Project phasing.** Plan capital spend across the periods it will occur.


-


**Excel flexibility.** Let contributors stay in spreadsheets if that is how they work.


-


**Security.** Look for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications.

## How to compare cost across vendors


Several FP&A vendors quote pricing on request. Ask each one for a written quote, and use the same questions for every vendor so the totals compare fairly:


-


**Licensing model.** Is pricing by user, entity, revenue band, data volume, or module?


-


**Operations access.** Do operations leaders who only view approved budgets need paid seats?


-


**Implementation.** Who does the work, how long does it take, and what is included? We guide implementation with in-house FP&A experts rather than third-party consultants.


-


**Training and support.** What is included, and what costs extra as your team grows?


-


**Connectors.** Are the ERP, HRIS, and CRM connectors you need included?


-


**Renewal terms.** What changes at renewal and as you add entities?


Then compare total cost of ownership over several years against the value of the time you save. Our[business budgeting software buyer's guide](https://www.abacum.ai/blog/business-budgeting-software-buyers-guide) covers a full evaluation framework.


## How to share approved budgets with operations


1.


**Decide what each role needs.** Department leaders typically need approved CapEx and OpEx by category, remaining budget, and spend to date. They do not need other departments' budgets.


2.


**Set role-based permissions.** Give each leader access to their own lines.


3.


**Publish after approval.** Make sure approved allocations reach operations as soon as finance finalizes them.


4.


**Keep actuals live.** Connect to your ERP so remaining budget reflects what has been spent.


5.


**Update as forecasts change.** When the plan is revised, operations should see the new numbers.


[AI Modeler](https://www.abacum.ai/blog/ai-modeler) can help here too. Ask it in plain language to add a variable to your OpEx model and break it down by a new dimension, such as channel, and it sets up the dimension and updates the totals for you to approve. It works inside your existing permissions, so it cannot read or change anything a user could not already read or change manually.


For planning cycles, connect this to your[annual operating plan](https://www.abacum.ai/blog/annual-operating-plan) so the approved plan flows into daily decisions.
